title: Covering-transfer hom (surjective + injective-on-G) unifies F4, F10, F11 via one injectivity hypothesis
evidence: The connection has two layers. (1) ORGANIZATIONAL CLAIM (verified TRUE by code inspection): one InjOn-form gadget really does underlie three in-tree results. sumsetDistinct_image_eq_univ (CoveringTransfer.lean:56) requires exactly Set.InjOn f G + surjectivity; image_sumsetDistinct_subset (:38) is the distinctness-preserving image step. markedCurveDecodable_interleaved_of_choose_le (GG25ExactPreservation.lean:175) is the curve-side analogue (proper-subspace covering, C(a,b)<=q). The F10/Loop52 cyclotomic side (subsetSum_injective_of_noRelation, not_dvd_collisionResultant, DISPROOF_LOG.md:1085-1135) is also an InjOn hypothesis on Z[zeta_n]->F_p, p not dividing Res(f_S-f_T, Phi_{2^mu}). All three genuinely share Set.InjOn structure. (2) PRIZE-RELEVANCE CLAIM (REFUTED by probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C088_v2.py, exact integer arithmetic, proper-subgroup prize primes). Diagnostic 1: in the prize regime mu_n is a PROPER subgroup of F_q* of size n=2^mu, so the covering CONCLUSION 'distinct sumset = F_q' is vacuous/false: #(all subset sums of mu_n mod q) = 81 for n=8/q=4129 and 6561 for n=16/q=65537, vs q ~ n^4 (bounded by 2^n << q). Diagnostic 2: across many fully-split prize primes q==1 mod n (n=8,16,32; beta=log_n q ~ 3), EVERY ONE satisfies the Res/injectivity condition trivially (zeta_n is a genuine root mod q), yet the actual prize quantity B = max_{b!=0}|sum_{y in mu_n} psi(by)| ranges B/sqrt(n) in [2.32, 4.20] (e.g. n=32 q=32993 spikes to 4.198), all well above the Ramanujan 2*sqrt(n). So injectivity-of-the-reduction is generic and DECOUPLED from whether B is small. Reason: injectivity is a SEPARATION/distinctness property of subset sums; the prize core (BGK) is a CANCELLATION property of additive characters psi(b*y) -- orthogonal quantities.
wall: W-idealSVP (the fully-split / Pan-Xu split-prime case the connection names as F11). The unified injectivity hypothesis is the separation half (distinct subset sums survive the reduction), which in the fully-split prize regime is generic and carries no character-cancellation information; the BGK sqrt-cancellation house B remains the untouched 25-year-open core. Also welds to W-Mersenne via the unchanged Conj 1.12 large-prime-factor input.
honest_note: The organizational insight is real and correct: one InjOn-form gadget genuinely abstracts CoveringTransfer + GG25ExactPreservation + the F10 cyclotomic-resultant injectivity (worth keeping as a unifying lemma). But the connection's load-bearing prize claim -- that this single injectivity hypothesis is 'the relevant hom for the prize' -- does not survive the prize regime. (a) The covering CONCLUSION needs a 2^mu-element domain whose subset sums are super-polynomially many; that is a char-0 / power-independent (Phi_n irreducible) phenomenon. In the prize's fully-split q==1 mod n regime the power basis COLLAPSES (zeta_n in F_q), mu_n is a finite subgroup of size only n, and the covering is impossible -- exactly the Loop49 honest correction already recorded in DISPROOF_LOG.md:1059-1066. (b) Injectivity/Res is generic and decoupled from B (Diagnostic 2). So PARTIAL: organizational sub-claim PROVEN, prize-relevance sub-claim REFUTED, net effect on the open core = none. No closure attempted or implied. Probes are exact integer/complex arithmetic at proper-subgroup primes (avoids the #400 full-group trap); B computed via exact mu-coset transversal scan. Not shown: I did not formalize the unifying abstract lemma in Lean (the attack_plan's optional DistinctnessPreservingTransfer) -- it would compile but adds nothing to the prize.
